editorial.headline: Soy-Sauce Manufacturing With a Clear PMA Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10771 covers soy-based kecap and taoco production, open across business scales and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under this record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10771 is a manufacturing activity for kecap: the production of soy sauce made from soybeans or other legumes. Its scope also reaches taoco, whether made from fresh soybeans or other legumes, or from residual material left over from kecap production. In plain English, this is the industrial classification for businesses turning legumes into fermented or processed soy-condiment products, with the record drawing the boundary around kecap and taoco rather than the broader universe of sauces.

The registration picture is unusually straightforward. The activity is open to every scale listed in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the classification is not reserved only for a large factory or only for a household-scale producer. It can describe a small production operation, a growing mid-sized processor, or a larger industrial setup, provided the registered business activity is genuinely the making of kecap or taoco from the materials described in the scope.

Nationally, the foreign-investment status is also clear. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Rendered practically, that is a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling at the national level. There is no lower foreign-share cap in this slim record, and no additional national threshold, licence, capital floor, or timing rule is supplied here. The honest reading is therefore limited and precise: as a national PMA classification, this activity is open up to full foreign ownership according to the fields provided.

Bali does not change that conclusion into a block in this record. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and l4_bali_blocked is false. The stated reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The moratorium rule itself says Bali blocks all Low plus Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently, but this record does not place KBLI 10771 inside that blocked result. The key point is that this activity is nationally open and not blocked in Bali, but only within the limits of the record itself.
